holidays.law: Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971 s.1(1) and Sch 1 para 1 (Easter Monday, last Monday in May, last Monday in August, 26 December if not a Sunday, 27 December in a year in which 25 or 26 December is a Sunday); New Year's Day, the early May bank holiday and the other weekend substitute days are appointed each year by royal proclamation under s.1(2) and (3) (proclamations of 9 July 2025 for 2026 and 8 July 2026 for 2027); Christmas Day and Good Friday are not bank holidays under the Act in England and Wales but are listed by gov.uk; s.1(4): a payment or act due on a bank holiday may be made on the next day it can be required

one_off.name_pl: Święto platynowego jubileuszu królowej Elżbiety II

one_off.name_pl: Dzień państwowego pogrzebu królowej Elżbiety II

court.title: Civil court proceedings (Civil Procedure Rules)
court.met_by: filing at the court office; an email recorded as received from 4pm to 11.59pm counts as filed on the next day the court office is open (PD 5B para 4.2); a Money Claim Online form received after 4pm counts on the next day the Civil National Business Centre is open (PD 7C para 5.2B); CE-File: the time on the submission confirmation, or when the fee is paid for a document that needs one (PD 5C para 3.5)
court.note: CPR 2.8(2) to (5) and 2.10: clear days; periods of 5 days or less skip Saturdays, Sundays, bank holidays, Christmas Day and Good Friday; a step at the court office due on a day the office is closed is in time on the next day it is open (this does not move service on the other party)

tax.title: HMRC time limits
tax.law: Taxes Management Act 1970 (no provision moves a deadline)
tax.met_by: an online return submitted by 11:59pm on the last day (gov.uk); a payment that has reached HMRC's account by the deadline (Faster Payments same or next day, including weekends; Bacs 3 working days; for a weekend or bank holiday deadline, other methods must arrive on the last working day before); a cheque counts on the day HMRC receives it if paid on first presentation (TMA 1970 s.70A)
tax.note: TMA 1970 s.8(1D), s.31A, s.59A(2), s.59B(4): dates and periods with no provision moving a deadline that falls on a weekend or bank holiday

administrative.title: Tribunals and other public bodies whose rules move a deadline
administrative.law: First-tier Tribunal procedure rules, r.12 (Social Entitlement Chamber 2008; Tax Chamber 2009)
administrative.met_by: received by the tribunal by 5pm (Social Entitlement Chamber r.12(1)) or before 5pm (Tax Chamber r.12(1)) on the last day
administrative.note: Tribunal Procedure (First-tier Tribunal) (Social Entitlement Chamber) Rules 2008 r.12(2) and (3); Tribunal Procedure (First-tier Tribunal) (Tax Chamber) Rules 2009 r.12(2) and (3); other bodies only where their own rules say so

civil.title: Contracts and consumer law
civil.law: no general rule moves the end of a period; Interpretation Act 1978 s.5 and Sch 1 ('month')
civil.met_by: as the contract or the statute provides; a consumer's cancellation of a distance or off-premises contract is in time if sent before the period ends (Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 reg 32(5))
civil.note: No general statutory rule moves the end of a contractual or consumer period; the contract or the specific statute decides; in legislation 'month' means calendar month (Interpretation Act 1978 s.5 and Sch 1)

deemed_delivery.title: Claim form served in the UK (County Court or High Court)
deemed_delivery.from: completion of the step under CPR 7.5(1): posting by First Class or next-business-day service, delivering or leaving it at the address, personal service, or sending the email
deemed_delivery.note: Deemed served on the second business day after the step; business days exclude Saturdays, Sundays, bank holidays, Good Friday and Christmas Day, so a step taken on a Friday gives the Tuesday. The defendant's response windows run from this date (CPR 10.3, 15.4).

deemed_delivery.title: Court document other than a claim form, sent by First Class post or next-business-day service
deemed_delivery.from: posting, or leaving with or collection by the delivery service
deemed_delivery.note: The second day after posting if that is a business day; otherwise the next business day after it. Posted on a Thursday: the Saturday is not a business day, so the Monday.

deemed_delivery.title: Court document other than a claim form, delivered to or left at the permitted address
deemed_delivery.note: That day if it is a business day and before 4.30pm; otherwise the next business day.

deemed_delivery.title: Court document other than a claim form, sent by email or another electronic method
deemed_delivery.note: That day if sent on a business day before 4.30pm; otherwise the next business day.

deemed_delivery.title: Court document other than a claim form, served personally
deemed_delivery.note: That day if before 4.30pm on a business day; otherwise the next business day.

deemed_delivery.title: Notice served by post under an Act, such as an HMRC or council notice with no day count of its own
deemed_delivery.law: Interpretation Act 1978 s.7; TMA 1970 s.115(2); Local Government Act 1972 s.233(2) and (4)
deemed_delivery.note: Served by properly addressing, prepaying and posting; delivered when it would arrive in the ordinary course of post, unless the contrary is proved. Royal Mail routing times are D+1 working day for First Class and D+3 for Second Class (Postal Services (Universal Postal Service) Order 2012 Sch 1 paras 2 and 3); days is the First Class minimum. HMRC manuals differ (EM1506: 1 and up to 3 working days; SAM31030: 2 and 4). Many HMRC windows run from the date of issue instead (TMA 1970 s.31A).

deemed_delivery.title: Council penalty charge notice, notice to owner or charge certificate sent by post (England)
deemed_delivery.law: Civil Enforcement of Road Traffic Contraventions (Approved Devices, Charging Guidelines and General Provisions) (England) Regulations 2022 reg 3(2) to (4)
deemed_delivery.note: First Class post only. Served on the second working day after posting; working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays, New Year's Day, Good Friday, Christmas Day and other bank holidays in England and Wales. The discount, payment and representation periods run from this date.

deemed_delivery.title: Private parking notice to keeper sent by post
deemed_delivery.law: Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 Sch 4 paras 8(6) and 9(6)
deemed_delivery.note: Presumed delivered on the second working day after posting, unless the contrary is proved; working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays in England and Wales.

deemed_delivery.title: Notice of intended prosecution or request to name the driver, sent by post (England and Wales)
deemed_delivery.law: Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 s.1(1ZA) and (1ZB); Road Traffic Act 1988 s.172(7) and (7A); Criminal Procedure Rules 2025 r.4.11(2)(b) and (3)
deemed_delivery.note: Served on the second business day after posting, unless something different is shown. A letter produced by a computer system for posting is taken as posted First Class on the business day after it was produced.

deemed_delivery.title: DWP decision on Universal Credit, PIP, new-style JSA or ESA sent by post
deemed_delivery.law: Universal Credit, Personal Independence Payment, Jobseeker's Allowance and Employment and Support Allowance (Decisions and Appeals) Regulations 2013 reg 2 ('the date of notification') and reg 3(2)
deemed_delivery.note: Treated as given on the day it is posted to the last known address, so the one-month window for mandatory reconsideration starts that day. A letter to DWP counts on the day DWP receives it (reg 3(1)).

response_windows.title: Acknowledgment of service of a County Court claim
response_windows.from: service of the particulars of claim (or of the claim form, when the particulars came with it)
response_windows.note: Clear days. Filing it extends the time for the defence to 28 days (CPR 15.4(1)(b)). Without an acknowledgment, defence or admission in time, the claimant may ask for default judgment (CPR 10.2, Part 12). Filing due on a day the court office is closed moves to the next open day (CPR 2.8(5)).

response_windows.title: Defence to a County Court claim, when no acknowledgment of service was filed
response_windows.from: service of the particulars of claim

response_windows.title: Defence to a County Court claim after filing an acknowledgment of service
response_windows.from: service of the particulars of claim

response_windows.title: Longest extension of the defence period the parties may agree (the defendant tells the court in writing)
response_windows.from: the end of the defence period under CPR 15.4
response_windows.law: CPR 15.5

response_windows.title: Claimant serves particulars of claim that the claim form said would follow
response_windows.from: service of the claim form
response_windows.note: And no later than the latest time for serving the claim form: midnight on the calendar day four months after its issue.

response_windows.title: Appeal to HMRC against an amendment of a return, a closure notice or an assessment
response_windows.from: the date the notice was issued (not the date it arrived)
response_windows.note: In writing, to the officer named on the notice, stating the grounds.

response_windows.title: Appeal against an HMRC late-filing or late-payment penalty
response_windows.from: the date the penalty notice was issued
response_windows.law: Finance Act 2009 Sch 55 paras 20 and 21, Sch 56 paras 13 and 14; TMA 1970 s.31A
response_windows.note: gov.uk: usually 30 days from the date the penalty was issued; a later appeal must give a reason.

response_windows.title: Pay an HMRC late-filing or late-payment penalty
response_windows.from: the day the penalty notice was issued
response_windows.law: Finance Act 2009 Sch 55 para 18(2), Sch 56 para 11(2)
response_windows.note: An appeal does not require the penalty to be paid before the appeal is decided (Sch 55 para 21(2)(a), Sch 56 para 14(2)(a)).

response_windows.title: Query an HMRC simple assessment (tax calculated without a return)
response_windows.from: the date the notice of assessment was issued
response_windows.note: HMRC may allow longer (s.31AA(3)(b)).

response_windows.title: Appeal against a simple assessment after HMRC's final response to the query
response_windows.from: the date HMRC gives notice of its final response

response_windows.title: Self Assessment return when HMRC's notice to file was given after 31 October
response_windows.from: the date of the notice

response_windows.title: Amend a Self Assessment return
response_windows.from: the filing date (31 January after the tax year, or the end of the 3-month period after a late notice)
response_windows.law: TMA 1970 s.9ZA(2) and (3)

response_windows.title: Claim back overpaid income tax or Capital Gains Tax (overpayment relief) and other claims for relief
response_windows.from: the end of the tax year concerned (5 April)
response_windows.law: TMA 1970 s.43(1), Sch 1AB para 3(1)

response_windows.title: Request mandatory reconsideration of a benefit decision (DWP; HMRC for Child Benefit)
response_windows.from: the date of notification of the decision (for Universal Credit, PIP, new-style JSA and ESA, the day the letter was posted)
response_windows.law: Universal Credit, Personal Independence Payment, Jobseeker's Allowance and Employment and Support Allowance (Decisions and Appeals) Regulations 2013 regs 2, 3 and 5(1)(b); Child Benefit: Child Benefit and Guardian's Allowance (Decisions and Appeals) Regulations 2003 reg 5(2)(b), as amended by SI 2023/179; other benefits outside the 2013 Regulations: Social Security and Child Support (Decisions and Appeals) Regulations 1999 reg 3(1)(b)
response_windows.met_by: the request being received by DWP (or HMRC) within the period (2013 regulations reg 3(1) and reg 5(1)(b))
response_windows.note: 14 days more when a written statement of reasons was asked for within the month (2013 regulations reg 5(1)(b)(ii) and (iii)); later requests only as regulation 6 allows.

response_windows.title: Appeal to the First-tier Tribunal (Social Security and Child Support) after mandatory reconsideration
response_windows.from: the date the mandatory reconsideration notice was sent
response_windows.law: Tribunal Procedure (First-tier Tribunal) (Social Entitlement Chamber) Rules 2008 r.22(2)(d)(i), r.12
response_windows.met_by: the notice of appeal being received by the tribunal by 5pm on the last day (r.12(1), r.22(2))
response_windows.note: A last day that is not a working day moves to the next working day (r.12(2)). A late appeal must ask for more time and give the reason (r.22(6)).

response_windows.title: Tell the council in writing that a council tax discount (such as the single person discount) no longer applies or is smaller
response_windows.from: the day there is first reason to believe the discount is wrong
response_windows.law: Council Tax (Administration and Enforcement) Regulations 1992 reg 16(1); Local Government Finance Act 1992 Sch 3 para 1(2)
response_windows.note: Failing to notify without reasonable excuse: penalty of £70 in England. Does not apply where council tax reduction reduces the liability other than to nil (reg 16(1A)). Wales has its own wording.

response_windows.title: Tell the council about a change that may affect council tax reduction (England)
response_windows.from: the day the change occurs
response_windows.law: Council Tax Reduction Schemes (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2012 Sch 8 para 9(2)
response_windows.note: Or as soon as reasonably practicable after the change, whichever is later; in writing, by telephone where the council allows it, or another way the council accepts. Wales has its own regulations.

response_windows.title: Appeal to the Valuation Tribunal for England on council tax liability, a discount or an exemption, after the council's decision
response_windows.from: service of the council's decision notice
response_windows.law: Valuation Tribunal for England (Council Tax and Rating Appeals) (Procedure) Regulations 2009 reg 21(2); Local Government Finance Act 1992 s.16
response_windows.note: The household writes to the council first. The Valuation Tribunal Service counts the 2 months from the date on the decision. The VTE President may accept a late appeal in limited cases (reg 21(6)).

response_windows.title: Appeal to the Valuation Tribunal for England when the council has not answered within 2 months
response_windows.from: service of the household's written notice to the council
response_windows.law: Valuation Tribunal for England (Council Tax and Rating Appeals) (Procedure) Regulations 2009 reg 21(3); Local Government Finance Act 1992 s.16

response_windows.title: Proposal to the Valuation Office Agency to change the council tax band, as a new taxpayer (England)
response_windows.from: the day the person first became the council taxpayer for the dwelling
response_windows.law: Council Tax (Alteration of Lists and Appeals) (England) Regulations 2009 reg 4(4) and (5)(a)

response_windows.title: Proposal after the Valuation Office Agency altered the band (England)
response_windows.from: service of the notice of alteration
response_windows.law: Council Tax (Alteration of Lists and Appeals) (England) Regulations 2009 reg 4(6)

response_windows.title: Valuation Office Agency decides on a council tax band proposal (England)
response_windows.from: the day the proposal was served
response_windows.law: Council Tax (Alteration of Lists and Appeals) (England) Regulations 2009 reg 9(1)

response_windows.title: Appeal to the Valuation Tribunal for England against the VOA's decision on a band proposal
response_windows.from: the day the decision notice was served on the proposer
response_windows.law: Council Tax (Alteration of Lists and Appeals) (England) Regulations 2009 reg 10(1) and (2)
response_windows.note: The VTE President may allow a later appeal for circumstances beyond the appellant's control (reg 10(3)). Wales: Valuation Tribunal for Wales, within 4 months (gov.uk).

response_windows.title: Pay a council penalty charge notice at the discounted amount (England)
response_windows.from: service of the penalty charge notice
response_windows.law: Civil Enforcement of Road Traffic Contraventions (Approved Devices, Charging Guidelines and General Provisions) (England) Regulations 2022 reg 2 ('the applicable date' (b)), Sch 2 paras 2(e) and 3(1)(e)
response_windows.note: The discount amount is set under the Traffic Management Act 2004 Sch 9. Parking anywhere in England; bus lane and moving traffic contraventions outside London.

response_windows.title: Pay a camera penalty charge notice sent by post at the discounted amount (England)
response_windows.from: service of the penalty charge notice
response_windows.law: 2022 General Regulations reg 2 ('the applicable date' (a)), reg 10(2)(a)

response_windows.title: Pay a penalty charge notice fixed to the vehicle or handed over (England)
response_windows.from: the day of the contravention
response_windows.law: 2022 General Regulations Sch 2 para 2(d), reg 20(1) and (2)
response_windows.note: Unpaid after that, the council may serve a notice to owner on the registered keeper, within 6 months.

response_windows.title: Pay a penalty charge notice sent by post (England)
response_windows.from: service of the penalty charge notice
response_windows.law: 2022 General Regulations Sch 2 para 3(1)(d) and (f)
response_windows.note: If no representations are made and the charge is not paid, the council may add the surcharge and enforce.

response_windows.title: Representations to the council against a notice to owner or a postal penalty charge notice (England)
response_windows.from: service of the notice
response_windows.law: Civil Enforcement of Road Traffic Contraventions (Representations and Appeals) (England) Regulations 2022 regs 5 and 6(2)
response_windows.note: Later representations may be disregarded. The grounds are listed in reg 5(4); compelling reasons may also be given (reg 5(2)(b)(ii)).

response_windows.title: Council decides on representations against a penalty charge (England)
response_windows.from: the council receiving the representations
response_windows.law: 2022 Appeals Regulations reg 6(3), (4) and (7)
response_windows.silence: no decision notice within the 56 days means the representations are accepted; the council cancels the notice and refunds any payment (reg 6(7))

response_windows.title: Appeal to the adjudicator after the council rejects representations (London Tribunals in London; Traffic Penalty Tribunal elsewhere in England)
response_windows.from: service of the notice of rejection
response_windows.law: 2022 Appeals Regulations reg 7(2); gov.uk Appeal against a penalty charge notice
response_windows.note: The adjudicator may allow a longer period (reg 7(2)(b)). If the charge is neither paid nor appealed, a charge certificate may follow (2022 General Regulations reg 21).

response_windows.title: Private parking operator delivers the notice to keeper when no notice was given at the car park
response_windows.from: the day the parking period ended
response_windows.law: Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 Sch 4 para 9(4) to (6)
response_windows.note: A condition of keeper liability. The period begins with the day after the parking ended; a posted notice is presumed delivered on the second working day after posting. After a windscreen notice, the notice to keeper is due within the 28 days that follow the first 28 days (para 8(4) and (5)).

response_windows.title: Keeper pays a private parking charge or names the driver before the operator can recover it from the keeper
response_windows.from: the day the notice to keeper was given
response_windows.law: Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 Sch 4 paras 8(2)(f) and 9(2)(f)
response_windows.note: The period begins with the day after the notice is given; a posted notice is presumed given on the second working day after posting (paras 8(6), 9(6)).

response_windows.title: Police serve a notice of intended prosecution (speeding and other listed offences) on the driver or registered keeper
response_windows.from: the offence
response_windows.law: Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 s.1(1), (1ZA) and (3), s.2(1) and (2)
response_windows.note: Not needed if the driver was warned at the time, a summons was served within the 14 days, an accident happened owing to the vehicle's presence on the road, or a fixed penalty notice was given. Compliance is presumed unless the contrary is proved (s.1(3)).

response_windows.title: Reply to a police request to name the driver (section 172 notice)
response_windows.from: the day the notice was served
response_windows.law: Road Traffic Act 1988 s.172(2), (3) and (7)
response_windows.note: Failing to give the information is an offence, with defences in s.172(4) and (7)(b).

response_windows.title: Pay a fixed penalty under a conditional offer (for example a speed camera offence)
response_windows.from: the date the conditional offer was issued
response_windows.law: Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 s.75(7)(c)
response_windows.note: The offer may state a longer period.

response_windows.title: Suspended enforcement period of a fixed penalty notice given by an officer (the time to pay)
response_windows.from: the date of the notice
response_windows.law: Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 s.52(3)(a)
response_windows.note: The statutory minimum; the notice may state a longer period, and the notice controls.

response_windows.title: Report an authorised push payment (APP) fraud to the bank for reimbursement
response_windows.from: the fraudulent payment
response_windows.law: Payment Systems Regulator Specific Direction 20 (Faster Payments) and Specific Direction 21 (CHAPS); PSR page 'APP fraud reimbursement protections'
response_windows.note: Payments made from 7 Oct 2024 by individuals, microenterprises and charities; maximum £85,000 per claim; optional excess of up to £100, not for vulnerable customers.

response_windows.title: Bank reimburses an authorised push payment (APP) fraud claim
response_windows.from: the customer's claim
response_windows.law: Payment Systems Regulator Specific Directions 20 and 21; PSR page 'APP fraud reimbursement protections'
response_windows.note: If the bank stops the clock to gather information, it must reach an outcome within 35 business days. A dispute can then go to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

response_windows.title: Cancelling goods bought online, by phone or away from the trader's premises (right to cancel)
response_windows.from: the day the goods come into the physical possession of the household or a person it named (not the carrier); for one order delivered in parts, the last part; for regular deliveries, the first
response_windows.law: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 reg. 29(1), 30(3) to (6), 32(5)
response_windows.met_by: sending a clear statement of cancellation, or the model form, before the end of the last day (reg. 32(5)); in a dispute the household must show it cancelled in time (reg. 32(6))
response_windows.note: Exceptions in reg. 28, such as personalised goods, goods that go off quickly, and sealed hygiene goods, recordings or software once unsealed.

response_windows.title: Cancelling a service, or digital content not on a physical medium, bought online, by phone or away from the trader's premises (right to cancel)
response_windows.from: the day the contract is entered into
response_windows.law: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 reg. 29(1), 30(2), 32(5)
response_windows.met_by: sending a clear statement of cancellation before the end of the last day (reg. 32(5))
response_windows.note: A service started early at the household's express request is paid for up to the cancellation (reg. 36(4)); the right ends once the service is fully performed after the household acknowledged that (reg. 36(2)). Digital content: the right ends once supply starts with the household's consent and acknowledgement (reg. 37(2)).

response_windows.title: Right to cancel when the trader never gave the cancellation information (extended cancellation period)
response_windows.from: the day the normal 14-day cancellation period would have ended
response_windows.law: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 reg. 31(1) and (3)
response_windows.met_by: sending a clear statement of cancellation before the end of the last day (reg. 32(5))
response_windows.note: If the trader gives the information within those 12 months, the period instead ends 14 days after the household receives it (reg. 31(2)).

response_windows.title: Trader refunds all payments, including standard delivery, after a cancellation
response_windows.from: the trader receiving the goods back or, if earlier, the household supplying evidence of having sent them; where the trader offered to collect, or there are no goods, the trader being informed of the cancellation
response_windows.law: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 reg. 34(1) to (6)
response_windows.met_by: the trader making the refund by the same means of payment, without a fee (reg. 34(7) and (8))
response_windows.note: The trader may deduct for handling beyond what is needed to check the goods, as a shop would allow (reg. 34(9) to (12)).

response_windows.title: Household sends the goods back after cancelling
response_windows.from: the day the household informs the trader of the cancellation
response_windows.law: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 reg. 35(2) and (4)
response_windows.met_by: sending off or handing over the goods before the end of the last day (reg. 35(4))
response_windows.note: Not needed when the trader offered to collect (reg. 35(1)). The household pays the direct return cost unless the trader agreed to pay or did not say the household pays (reg. 35(5) to (7)).

response_windows.title: Rejecting faulty goods for a full refund (short-term right to reject)
response_windows.from: the last of: ownership (or possession under hire) passing, delivery, and the trader saying installation is done
response_windows.law: Consumer Rights Act 2015 s. 19(3), 20, 22(3)
response_windows.met_by: the household indicating clearly to the trader that it rejects the goods (s. 20(5) and (6))
response_windows.note: Goods expected to perish sooner: the period ends when they could be expected to perish (s. 22(4)). The days stop while the household waits for a repair or replacement it asked for or agreed to; if that fails, at least 7 days remain (s. 22(6) to (8)).

response_windows.title: Trader refunds after the household rejects faulty goods
response_windows.from: the day the trader agrees that the household is entitled to a refund
response_windows.law: Consumer Rights Act 2015 s. 20(15) to (17)
response_windows.met_by: the trader giving the refund by the same means of payment, without a fee (s. 20(16) and (17))
response_windows.note: A price reduction for a poor service is refunded on the same terms (s. 56(4)).

response_windows.title: A fault that shows within this period is taken to have existed at delivery (for repair, replacement, price reduction and final rejection)
response_windows.from: the day the goods were delivered
response_windows.law: Consumer Rights Act 2015 s. 19(14) and (15)
response_windows.note: Not when the trader shows the goods conformed, or when this does not fit the goods or the fault. Digital content: 6 months from supply (s. 42(9) and (10)).

response_windows.title: Final right to reject used in this period: no deduction for use (motor vehicles excepted)
response_windows.from: the last of: ownership passing, delivery, and the trader saying installation is done
response_windows.law: Consumer Rights Act 2015 s. 24(8) to (12)
response_windows.note: The final right to reject, or a price reduction, is available only after one failed repair or replacement, when neither is possible, or when the trader did not do it within a reasonable time (s. 24(5)).

response_windows.title: Time limit for a court claim on a contract, including faulty goods and poor services (limitation)
response_windows.from: the date the cause of action accrued, usually the breach such as delivery of faulty goods
response_windows.law: Limitation Act 1980 s. 5
response_windows.note: A contract made by deed: 12 years (s. 8). A sum recoverable by statute, such as the penalty for an unprotected tenancy deposit: 6 years (s. 9). Court steps follow the court rules.

response_windows.title: Bank's, insurer's or other financial firm's response to a complaint (final response)
response_windows.from: the firm receiving the complaint
response_windows.law: FCA Handbook DISP 1.6.1R, 1.6.2R
response_windows.met_by: the firm sending a final response, or a written reply explaining why it needs longer and telling the household it may now refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service (DISP 1.6.2R(1) and (2))
response_windows.silence: after 8 weeks without a final response the household may refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service (DISP 2.8.1R; FCA, How to complain)

response_windows.title: Response to a complaint about a payment service or e-money (transfer, card payment, direct debit)
response_windows.from: the firm receiving the complaint
response_windows.law: FCA Handbook DISP 1.6.2AR(1); Payment Services Regulations 2017 reg. 101(5) for complainants outside the ombudsman's reach
response_windows.met_by: the firm sending a final response; in exceptional circumstances, a holding reply giving the reasons and a deadline of at most 35 business days (DISP 1.6.2AR(2))
response_windows.silence: without a final response or holding reply in time, the household may refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service (DISP 2.8.1R; FCA, How to complain)

response_windows.title: Final response to a payment-service or e-money complaint after a holding reply in exceptional circumstances
response_windows.from: the firm receiving the complaint
response_windows.law: FCA Handbook DISP 1.6.2AR(2); Payment Services Regulations 2017 reg. 101(6) and (7)
response_windows.met_by: the firm sending its final response by the deadline stated in the holding reply
response_windows.silence: the household may refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service (DISP 2.8.1R; FCA, How to complain)

response_windows.title: Referring a complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service after the firm's final response
response_windows.from: the date the firm sent its final response
response_windows.law: FCA Handbook DISP 2.8.2R(1)
response_windows.note: The ombudsman counts calendar months: a response sent on 7 May allows until 7 November, one sent on 30 August until 28 February. The final response must mention the 6 months. A late complaint may still be heard in exceptional circumstances, when the final response was not valid, or when the firm agrees. The complaint to the firm must generally be made within 6 years of the event or 3 years of becoming aware (DISP 2.8.2R(2)).

response_windows.title: Energy supplier's time to resolve a complaint before the Energy Ombudsman can take it
response_windows.from: the supplier receiving the complaint
response_windows.law: Gas and Electricity (Consumer Complaints Handling Standards) Regulations 2008 reg. 2 (specified time period) and 6; Energy Ombudsman rules
response_windows.met_by: the complaint resolved, or a deadlock letter that lets the household go to the Energy Ombudsman sooner
response_windows.silence: the supplier must send written notice of the right to refer the complaint to the Energy Ombudsman when the period ends (next working day if that is not a working day), and the household may then refer it (reg. 6(3))

response_windows.title: Taking an energy dispute to the Energy Ombudsman after a deadlock letter
response_windows.from: the household receiving the supplier's deadlock letter
response_windows.law: Energy Ombudsman rules (scheme rule, not statute)
response_windows.note: The Energy Ombudsman FAQ states this limit for deadlock letters; no limit was found for a referral after 8 weeks without a deadlock letter.

response_windows.title: Phone, broadband or pay-TV provider's time to resolve a complaint before it can go to ADR
response_windows.from: the complaint first being raised with the provider, for complaints raised on or after 8 April 2026
response_windows.law: Ofcom General Condition C4, as modified by Ofcom's statement of 8 July 2025 (in force 8 April 2026)
response_windows.met_by: the complaint resolved, or a deadlock letter that lets the household go to ADR sooner
response_windows.silence: the provider must tell the household of its right to ADR, and the household may take the complaint to the provider's ADR scheme, the Communications Ombudsman or CISAS (General Condition C4)
response_windows.note: 8 weeks for complaints raised before 8 April 2026.

response_windows.title: Leaving a phone, broadband or pay-TV contract without an early termination charge after the provider notifies a change to the household's disadvantage
response_windows.from: the provider's notification of the change
response_windows.law: Ofcom General Condition C1.14 to C1.16
response_windows.met_by: the household telling the provider within the month that it ends the contract
response_windows.note: Includes a price rise the contract does not set out; contracts made from 17 January 2025 must state any price rise in pounds and pence. The provider gives at least one month's notice on a durable medium. Leaving costs only service fees to the end date and any equipment kept. Changes solely to the household's benefit, purely administrative ones and those required by law are excluded.

response_windows.title: Maximum notice to end a phone, broadband or pay-TV contract that rolled on after its fixed term
response_windows.from: the provider receiving the household's notice
response_windows.law: Ofcom General Condition C1 (C1.21 and C1.22 in the October 2024 consolidated text)
response_windows.note: The household pays only the service fees for the notice period. A broadband or landline switch through One Touch Switch is arranged by the new provider, with no notice-period charges after the switch date (General Condition C7.8).

response_windows.title: Maximum notice to end an energy contract with no fixed term (evergreen contract)
response_windows.from: the supplier receiving the household's notice
response_windows.law: Electricity supply licence standard condition 24.6 and 24.7
response_windows.note: No notice is needed to end a fixed-term contract or to switch; no exit fee in the switching window, which starts at the earlier of the renewal statement and 49 days before the fixed term ends (standard condition 24.8 and 24.17).

response_windows.title: Cancelling a general insurance policy without penalty (cooling-off period)
response_windows.from: the day the policy is concluded, or the day the household receives the terms and conditions if later
response_windows.law: FCA Handbook ICOBS 7.1 (7.1.1R for the period)
response_windows.note: Exceptions include travel or baggage cover of less than one month. No reason is needed.

response_windows.title: Cancelling a life or other pure protection policy, or payment protection, without penalty (cooling-off period)
response_windows.from: the day the household is told the policy is concluded, or the day it receives the terms and conditions if later
response_windows.law: FCA Handbook ICOBS 7.1 (7.1.1R for the period)

response_windows.title: Landlord protects the tenancy deposit and gives the prescribed information
response_windows.from: the day the landlord receives the deposit
response_windows.law: Housing Act 2004 s. 213(3), (5) and (6)
response_windows.met_by: the deposit protected in an authorised scheme and the prescribed information given to the tenant
response_windows.silence: the tenant may apply to the county court, also after the tenancy ends; the court orders the deposit repaid or protected and the landlord to pay 1 to 3 times the deposit (s. 214)

response_windows.title: Landlord's gas safety check of each appliance and flue in a rented home
response_windows.from: the last safety check of that appliance or flue
response_windows.law: Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 reg. 36(3)(a)
response_windows.met_by: the check carried out and recorded

response_windows.title: Landlord gives existing tenants a copy of the gas safety record
response_windows.from: the date of the gas safety check
response_windows.law: Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 reg. 36(6)(a)
response_windows.met_by: the copy given to each existing tenant
response_windows.note: A new tenant gets the latest record before moving in (reg. 36(6)(b)).

response_windows.title: Landlord's inspection and test of the electrical installation in a rented home (electrical installation condition report)
response_windows.from: the last inspection and test, or an earlier date the last report sets
response_windows.law: Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector and Social Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 reg. 3(1)(b) and (2)(a)
response_windows.met_by: the inspection and test carried out by a qualified person

response_windows.title: Landlord gives existing tenants a copy of the electrical safety report
response_windows.from: the inspection and test
response_windows.law: Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector and Social Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 reg. 3(3)(b)
response_windows.met_by: the copy given to each existing tenant
response_windows.note: A new tenant gets the latest report before moving in; a prospective tenant within 28 days of a written request (reg. 3(3)(e)). Remedial work within 28 days, or sooner if the report says so (reg. 3(4)).

response_windows.title: Tenant's notice to end an assured periodic tenancy with a private landlord in England (notice to quit)
response_windows.from: the tenant giving the notice to the landlord
response_windows.law: Protection from Eviction Act 1977 s. 5(1), (1ZA) to (1ZD) and 5A, inserted by Renters' Rights Act 2025 s. 20 and 21 (in force 1 May 2026 for private tenancies, SI 2026/421 reg. 2)
response_windows.met_by: a notice in writing, by any means such as a letter, email or text, given at least 2 months before the date it is to take effect
response_windows.note: A shorter period is possible if the landlord agrees in writing (with all joint tenants). gov.uk ties the end date to the rent day (the day rent is due or the day before); see uncertain. One joint tenant can end the tenancy.

response_windows.title: Landlord's decision on a tenant's request to keep a pet
response_windows.from: the date of the tenant's request
response_windows.law: Housing Act 1988 s. 16A(1), inserted by Renters' Rights Act 2025 s. 11 (in force 1 May 2026 for private tenancies)
response_windows.met_by: the landlord giving the decision in writing on or before the 28th day after the request
response_windows.note: Extended to the 7th day after the tenant provides further information the landlord reasonably asked for, or after a superior landlord answers (s. 16A(2) and (3)), or to a date both agree (s. 16A(4)). Consent must not be unreasonably refused (s. 16A(1)(b)).

response_windows.title: Neighbour's consent to a party structure or excavation notice (party wall)
response_windows.from: the day the notice was served
response_windows.law: Party Wall etc. Act 1996 s. 5, 6(7)
response_windows.met_by: the neighbour serving a notice of consent
response_windows.silence: the neighbour is treated as dissenting and a dispute is treated as having arisen, to be settled under s. 10 (surveyors) (s. 5, 6(7))
response_windows.note: Notice periods for the building owner: 2 months before party structure work (s. 3(2)(a)); 1 month before excavation near the neighbour's building (s. 6(5)) or a new wall at the boundary (s. 1(2) and (5)).

response_windows.title: Social landlord investigates a potential significant damp and mould hazard (Awaab's Law)
response_windows.from: the day the landlord becomes aware of the issue
response_windows.law: Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025 (SI 2025/1042) reg. 6(4)
response_windows.met_by: the investigation completed
response_windows.note: Social housing in England only. Written summary within 3 working days after the investigation (reg. 9). Emergency hazards: action within 24 hours (reg. 5). More hazards planned from 30 November 2026.

response_windows.title: Claiming reimbursement from the bank for an authorised push payment scam (APP scam)
response_windows.from: the last payment in the scam
response_windows.law: Payment Systems Regulator APP scams reimbursement requirement (PS23/4; consolidated PS25/5)
response_windows.note: Faster Payments and CHAPS made on or after 7 October 2024; up to £85,000; an optional excess of up to £100, not for vulnerable customers. No reimbursement for someone complicit or grossly negligent; gross negligence does not apply to vulnerable customers.

response_windows.title: Bank pays an APP scam reimbursement claim
response_windows.from: the household making the claim
response_windows.law: Payment Systems Regulator APP scams reimbursement requirement (PS23/4; consolidated PS25/5)
response_windows.met_by: the bank paying the reimbursement; if it stops the clock to gather information, it reaches an outcome within 35 business days
response_windows.note: A dispute about the outcome goes to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

response_windows.title: Tell DVLA if the new vehicle log book (V5C) has not arrived; after this a replacement costs £25
response_windows.from: DVLA being told of the change of keeper or of the keeper's new address
response_windows.law: Guidance: gov.uk 'Sold, bought or transferred a vehicle' and 'Change the address on your vehicle log book (V5C)'; fee: Road Vehicles (Registration and Licensing) Regulations 2002 reg. 18(1A) and 22(3)
response_windows.note: DVLA asks to be contacted after 4 weeks. After an online notice by the seller the V5C usually arrives within 5 to 7 working days. The guidance has no rule for weekends or bank holidays, so the date is not moved.

response_windows.title: Contact DVLA if the automatic vehicle tax refund cheque has not arrived
response_windows.from: DVLA being told of the sale, transfer, SORN, scrapping or export
response_windows.law: Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994 s. 19(1), (3)(e) and (f), (3A) and (7); guidance: gov.uk 'Cancel your vehicle tax and get a refund'
response_windows.met_by: DVLA sending a refund cheque for each full month of tax left, counted from the date it got the information
response_windows.note: The 8 weeks come from gov.uk guidance, not from a statute. A vehicle tax Direct Debit is cancelled automatically.

response_windows.title: Register the birth with the registrar for the district where the baby was born (after 42 days the registrar can require a qualified informant to attend)
response_windows.from: the date of the birth
response_windows.law: Births and Deaths Registration Act 1953 s. 2(1) and s. 4
response_windows.note: The Act does not move the end date for weekends or bank holidays, and the day of birth is not counted ('from the date of the birth'). Child Benefit can be claimed 48 hours after registration (gov.uk).

response_windows.title: Claim Child Benefit; a claim reaches back at most 3 months, so claim within 3 months of the birth to be paid from the start
response_windows.from: the first day of entitlement, normally the birth
response_windows.law: Child Benefit and Guardian's Allowance (Administration) Regulations 2003 reg. 6(1); guidance: gov.uk 'Child Benefit: how to claim'
response_windows.note: The regulations count 3 months beginning with each day of entitlement and do not move the end date. Weekly rates from 6 Apr 2026: £27.05 for the eldest or only child, £17.90 for each other child (Child Benefit (Rates) Regulations 2006 reg. 2(1), sums from SI 2026/232).

response_windows.title: Claim the Sure Start Maternity Grant (£500; usually for a first child; a qualifying benefit such as Universal Credit is needed); claims open 11 weeks before the expected week of birth
response_windows.from: the birth (the actual date of confinement)
response_windows.law: Social Security (Claims and Payments) Regulations 1987 reg. 19(1), Sch. 4 para. 8(a); Social Fund Maternity and Funeral Expenses (General) Regulations 2005 reg. 5(1), (2) and (6)
response_windows.note: England and Wales only. The regulations do not move the end date.

response_windows.title: Take statutory paternity leave (one week, two weeks together, or two separate weeks); a right from the first day of employment since 6 Apr 2026
response_windows.from: the birth, or the first day of the expected week of birth when the baby is born early
response_windows.law: Paternity and Adoption Leave Regulations 2002 reg. 4, reg. 5(1) and (2) (qualifying period removed from 6 Apr 2026 by SI 2026/15)
response_windows.note: Notice of entitlement by the 15th week before the expected week of birth (reg. 6(3)); notice of each period at least 28 days before it, or as soon as reasonably practicable (reg. 6(4)). Statutory Paternity Pay still needs 26 weeks' service (Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992 s. 171ZA(2)).

response_windows.title: Opt out of the workplace pension the employer enrolled you in, with the scheme's opt-out notice given to the employer (contributions are refunded)
response_windows.from: the later of becoming an active member of the scheme and receiving the enrolment information (for a personal pension scheme: the date the agreement is treated as made)
response_windows.law: Pensions Act 2008 s. 8; Occupational and Personal Pension Schemes (Automatic Enrolment) Regulations 2010 reg. 9(2), (3) and (7)
response_windows.note: If the employer finds the notice invalid, it must say why and the period becomes 6 weeks (reg. 9(7)).

response_windows.title: Employer refunds the pension contributions after a valid opt-out
response_windows.from: the employer being given a valid opt-out notice
response_windows.law: Occupational and Personal Pension Schemes (Automatic Enrolment) Regulations 2010 reg. 11(1) and (3)
response_windows.met_by: the employer paying the refund to the jobholder before the refund date
response_windows.note: When payroll had already closed, the refund date is the last day of the second pay reference period after the notice (reg. 11(3)(b)).

response_windows.title: Register the death with the registrar (the 5 days run from the registrar being notified that the medical examiner confirmed the cause of death, not from the death)
response_windows.from: the relevant date: the registrar being notified that the medical examiner has confirmed the cause of death, or a coroner's investigation being discontinued
response_windows.law: Births and Deaths Registration Act 1953 s. 16(3) and (4), s. 17(3) and (4), s. 18
response_windows.note: Written notice of the death sent to the registrar with the medical certificate within the 5 days extends the time to 14 days from the relevant date (s. 18). The duty does not apply while a coroner's investigation continues. The Act does not move the end date.

response_windows.title: Use the Tell Us Once reference number from the registrar (reports the death to HMRC, DWP, HM Passport Office, DVLA and the council)
response_windows.from: the registrar giving the reference number at registration
response_windows.law: Guidance: gov.uk 'What to do after someone dies: Tell Us Once' (no statute)
response_windows.note: After expiry the registrar may not issue a new number, and each organisation must be told directly. The guidance does not move the end date.

response_windows.title: Pay the Inheritance Tax due on the death; interest runs after this date
response_windows.from: the end of the month in which the death occurred
response_windows.law: Inheritance Tax Act 1984 s. 226(1) and (2); instalments for land, some shares and businesses s. 227(1)
response_windows.note: Example: a death on 10 March gives a due date of 30 September. Personal representatives pay their tax when they deliver the account (s. 226(2)), and the estate's value is reported before probate (gov.uk).

response_windows.title: Personal representatives deliver the Inheritance Tax account (IHT400), unless the estate is an excepted estate
response_windows.from: the end of the month in which the death occurred
response_windows.law: Inheritance Tax Act 1984 s. 216(1) and (6)(a); Inheritance Tax (Delivery of Accounts) (Excepted Estates) Regulations 2004 reg. 3(1) and 4
response_windows.note: If it ends later, the deadline is 3 months from the date the personal representatives first act as such (s. 216(6)(a)). Probate cannot be applied for until the estate's value is reported (gov.uk 'Applying for probate').

response_windows.title: Claim Bereavement Support Payment to receive the one-off payment and all 18 monthly payments
response_windows.from: the date of the partner's death
response_windows.law: Social Security (Claims and Payments) Regulations 1987 reg. 19(2) and (3)(gb); Bereavement Support Payment Regulations 2017 reg. 3; guidance: gov.uk 'Bereavement Support Payment: what you'll get'
response_windows.note: Rates confirmed from 6 Apr 2026 (SI 2026/148 art. 19): higher rate £3,500 then 18 payments of £350; standard rate £2,500 then 18 payments of £100. A later claim loses earlier monthly payments; after 21 months usually nothing is paid (gov.uk). The regulations count 3 months beginning with each day of entitlement and do not move the end date.

response_windows.title: Claim Bereavement Support Payment in time to keep the one-off first payment
response_windows.from: the date of the spouse's, civil partner's or cohabiting partner's death
response_windows.law: Social Security (Claims and Payments) Regulations 1987 reg. 19(3BA); Bereavement Support Payment Regulations 2017 reg. 3(2) and (5)
response_windows.note: A claim more than 12 months after the death can still bring some monthly payments up to 21 months (gov.uk), but not the one-off payment. The regulations do not move the end date.

response_windows.title: Claim a Funeral Expenses Payment (Social Fund), possible from the date of death, even while waiting for a decision on a qualifying benefit
response_windows.from: the date of the funeral
response_windows.law: Social Security (Claims and Payments) Regulations 1987 reg. 19(1), Sch. 4 para. 9; guidance: gov.uk 'Funeral Expenses Payment: how to claim'
response_windows.note: For a person on a qualifying benefit who pays for the funeral; money the claimant gets from the deceased's estate is set against it (Social Fund Maternity and Funeral Expenses (General) Regulations 2005 reg. 10). The regulations do not move the end date.

response_windows.title: Reply to a subject access request, for example a GP surgery or hospital asked for copies of health records (free of charge)
response_windows.from: the latest of: the controller receiving the request, receiving identity information it asked for, and receiving any fee allowed
response_windows.law: UK GDPR Art. 12(3), (5) and (6), Art. 12A, Art. 15 (Art. 12A inserted by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 s. 76, in force 5 Feb 2026)
response_windows.met_by: the controller providing the information, or telling the person why it is not acting and how to complain
response_windows.note: The controller may extend by two further months for complex or numerous requests, by notice with reasons within the first month (Art. 12A(3) and (4)). The time stops while it waits for clarification it reasonably needs (Art. 12A(5)). The UK GDPR has no rule moving the end date.

response_windows.title: Have a prescription for a prescription-only medicine dispensed; a repeatable prescription must be dispensed for the first time within this period
response_windows.from: the appropriate date: for an NHS prescription, the later of the signing date and any 'not before' date the prescriber wrote
response_windows.law: Human Medicines Regulations 2012 reg. 217(5) and (7)
response_windows.note: Controlled drugs in Schedules 2, 3 and 4 have 28 days (prescription-controlled-drug).

response_windows.title: Have a prescription for a Schedule 2, 3 or 4 controlled drug dispensed (for instalments, the first instalment)
response_windows.from: the appropriate date: the later of the signing date and any 'not before' date the prescriber wrote
response_windows.law: Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001 reg. 16(1)(e), (4)(a), (5) and (7)

response_windows.title: Start of consultant-led treatment after a referral (England); if it will not happen in time, the patient can ask for an earlier appointment with another provider
response_windows.from: the start date: the day the provider received the referral
response_windows.law: National Health Service Commissioning Board and Clinical Commissioning Groups (Responsibilities and Standing Rules) Regulations 2012 reg. 44, 45(3), 46, 47 and 48; NHS Constitution for England
response_windows.met_by: treatment starting, or another event listed in reg. 46 that ends the waiting time
response_windows.silence: when the patient tells the provider or the integrated care board that treatment has not started or will not start within 18 weeks, the board (or NHS England) must take all reasonable steps to offer an earlier appointment with another suitable provider (reg. 47 and 48)
response_windows.note: England only. The 92% standard in reg. 45(3) binds the system, not each patient.

response_windows.title: Pay a school-absence penalty notice at the reduced amount of £80 (England; first notice for that child within 3 years)
response_windows.from: receiving the penalty notice
response_windows.law: Education Act 1996 s. 444A; Education (Penalty Notices) (England) Regulations 2007 reg. 4(2) to (4A) (as amended by SI 2024/210 and SI 2024/717, from 19 Aug 2024)
response_windows.note: After 21 days the penalty is £160. A second notice for the same child within 3 years is £160 with no reduction. The regulations do not move the end date.

response_windows.title: Last day to pay a school-absence penalty notice (£160 after the first 21 days) before the council prosecutes or withdraws the notice (England)
response_windows.from: receiving the penalty notice
response_windows.law: Education (Penalty Notices) (England) Regulations 2007 reg. 4(3)(b), reg. 5 (28 days since SI 2013/757) and reg. 9
response_windows.note: No third notice for the same parent and child within 3 years (reg. 12A); the council considers other action instead. The regulations do not move the end date.

recurring.title: Register for Self Assessment (notify HMRC of chargeability) for the tax year that ended on 5 April
recurring.applies_when: someone in the household had income or gains to declare for the last tax year (such as self-employment, rent or untaxed income) and has not filed a return before, or did not file for the year before
recurring.law: TMA 1970 s.7(1), (1A), (1C)(a), (3); Finance Act 2008 Sch 41 para 1

recurring.title: Self Assessment paper return for the tax year that ended on 5 April
recurring.applies_when: a household member files Self Assessment on paper

recurring.title: Online return by this date to have a Self Assessment balance under £3,000 collected through the PAYE tax code
recurring.applies_when: a household member who files online owes less than £3,000 and has PAYE income (a job or pension)
recurring.law: TMA 1970 s.59B(2)(b); gov.uk Pay your Self Assessment tax bill: through your tax code

recurring.title: Self Assessment online return for the previous tax year (by 11:59pm)
recurring.applies_when: a household member must file a Self Assessment return

recurring.title: Self Assessment balancing payment and, where payments on account apply, the first payment on account for the current tax year
recurring.applies_when: a household member owes tax under Self Assessment

recurring.title: Second Self Assessment payment on account
recurring.applies_when: payments on account apply: last year's Self Assessment bill was £1,000 or more and less than 80% of the tax was paid at source
recurring.law: TMA 1970 s.59A(1) and (2)(b); gov.uk Understand your Self Assessment tax bill: payments on account

recurring.title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax quarterly update (cumulative from 6 April)
recurring.applies_when: a sole trader or landlord must use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: qualifying income over £50,000 in 2024-25 (from April 2026), over £30,000 in 2025-26 (from April 2027) or over £20,000 in 2026-27 (from April 2028)
recurring.law: Income Tax (Digital Obligations) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/336) regs 9, 12 and 27

recurring.title: P60 for the tax year that ended on 5 April should have arrived from each employer or pension payer
recurring.applies_when: a household member was employed, or drew a pension taxed through PAYE, on 5 April
recurring.law: Income Tax (Pay As You Earn) Regulations 2003 reg 67(1)

recurring.title: P11D statement of benefits and expenses for the last tax year should have arrived
recurring.applies_when: an employer provides benefits or expenses reported on form P11D
recurring.law: Income Tax (Pay As You Earn) Regulations 2003 reg 94(1)

recurring.title: Last day to pay the High Income Child Benefit Charge for the previous tax year through PAYE; after it, Self Assessment is required
recurring.applies_when: Child Benefit is paid for a child in the household, a partner's adjusted net income was over £60,000 in the last tax year, and that partner has no other reason to file a return
recurring.law: Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003 ss.681B and 681C; gov.uk High Income Child Benefit Charge: pay through PAYE

recurring.title: New council tax year: check the bill (band, discounts, instalment dates set by the council) and register the instalments
recurring.applies_when: the household is liable for council tax
recurring.law: Local Government Finance Act 1992 s.30(6); Council Tax (Administration and Enforcement) Regulations 1992 regs 19 and 21, Sch 1 para 2(3), (3A) and (4)

recurring.title: Apply to the home council for a secondary school place for next September (common application form, England)
recurring.applies_when: a child in England moves to secondary school next September (normally a child now in year 6)
recurring.law: School Admissions (Admission Arrangements and Co-ordination of Admission Arrangements) (England) Regulations 2012 Sch. 2 para. 2(2)(a); School Admissions Code 2021

recurring.title: Apply to the home council for a primary school place for next September, for reception or a junior school (common application form, England)
recurring.applies_when: a child in England turns 4 by 31 August this year, or moves to a junior school next September
recurring.law: School Admissions (Admission Arrangements and Co-ordination of Admission Arrangements) (England) Regulations 2012 Sch. 2 para. 2(2)(a); School Admissions Code 2021 para. 2.17

recurring.title: National offer day for secondary school places (England); the next working day when 1 March is not a working day
recurring.applies_when: a secondary school application was made by 31 October
recurring.law: School Admissions (Admission Arrangements and Co-ordination of Admission Arrangements) (England) Regulations 2012 reg. 30(2)(b); School Admissions Code 2021 para. 2.12(b)

recurring.title: National offer day for primary school places (England); the next working day when 16 April is not a working day
recurring.applies_when: a primary school application was made by 15 January
recurring.law: School Admissions (Admission Arrangements and Co-ordination of Admission Arrangements) (England) Regulations 2012 reg. 30(2)(a); School Admissions Code 2021 para. 2.12(c)

recurring.title: Have the Free Childcare for Working Parents code in place by the end of the term before the hours start (hours from 1 January, 1 April or 1 September, England)
recurring.applies_when: working parents in England with a child aged 9 months to 4 years (or reaching 9 months in the next term) who want the funded hours
recurring.law: Childcare (Free of Charge for Working Parents) (England) Regulations 2022 reg. 25(1) and 27(1)(a); gov.uk 'Free Childcare for Working Parents: when to apply'

recurring.title: Tell HMRC that a young person who turned 16 is staying in full-time non-advanced education or approved training, or Child Benefit stops on 31 August
recurring.applies_when: the household gets Child Benefit for a young person whose 16th birthday falls between 1 September last year and 31 August this year
recurring.law: Child Benefit (General) Regulations 2006 reg. 3 and 4; gov.uk 'Child Benefit for children 16 to 19'

retention.title: Records behind a Self Assessment return without self-employment or letting (payslips, P60, P45, P11D, interest and dividend statements, Gift Aid and pension contribution records)
retention.title_pl: Dokumenty do zeznania Self Assessment bez działalności i najmu (paski płacowe, P60, P45, P11D, zestawienia odsetek i dywidend, dowody darowizn Gift Aid i składek emerytalnych)
retention.from: 31 January after the end of the tax year (the online filing date)
retention.note: About 22 months after the tax year ends. Longer while HMRC is enquiring into the return; for a return sent late, gov.uk says at least 15 months after sending it. Failing to keep records can cost a penalty of up to £3,000 (s.12B(5)).

retention.title: Records behind a Self Assessment return with self-employment, a partnership or letting income
retention.title_pl: Dokumenty do zeznania Self Assessment przy działalności, spółce osobowej lub dochodach z najmu
retention.from: 31 January after the end of the tax year (the online filing date)
retention.note: Letting property counts as carrying on a trade for this rule. Longer while HMRC is enquiring into the return. gov.uk example: records for a 2022-23 return filed by 31 January 2024 are kept until at least the end of January 2029.

retention.title: P60, P45, P11D statements and payslips of an employee or pensioner outside Self Assessment
retention.title_pl: Formularze P60, P45, P11D i paski płacowe pracownika lub emeryta rozliczanego bez zeznania Self Assessment
retention.from: the end of the tax year they relate to (5 April)
retention.note: No period is set for an employee outside Self Assessment. A claim for relief or overpaid tax can be made up to 4 years after the end of the tax year, and these documents support it. Anyone who files a return keeps them under TMA 1970 s.12B instead.

retention.title: Bank and building society statements
retention.title_pl: Wyciągi bankowe
retention.from: the period of the item they prove
retention.note: No period is set for a household. Keep a statement while it is the proof for another item in this list: 1 or 5 years after 31 January when it supports a tax return (TMA 1970 s.12B; gov.uk lists bank statements among records to keep); 6 years when it proves payment of a contract debt (Limitation Act 1980 s.5).

retention.title: Council tax bills (demand notices) and proof of payment
retention.title_pl: Rachunki za council tax (wezwania do zapłaty) i potwierdzenia zapłaty
retention.from: the date each instalment fell due
retention.law: Council Tax (Administration and Enforcement) Regulations 1992 reg 34(3)
retention.note: A council cannot apply for a liability order for a sum more than 6 years after it became due; the bills and proof of payment answer any claim of arrears within that time.

retention.title: Paid household bills and receipts under contracts (energy, phone, rent, purchases)
retention.title_pl: Opłacone rachunki domowe i potwierdzenia zapłaty z umów (energia, telefon, czynsz, zakupy)
retention.from: the payment
retention.note: Suggestion. A claim on a simple contract cannot be brought more than 6 years after the cause of action accrued; proof of payment answers a later claim for the same bill.

retention.title: Receipts, invoices, order confirmations and guarantees for goods and services
retention.title_pl: Paragony, faktury, potwierdzenia zamówień i gwarancje na towary i usługi
retention.from: delivery of the goods or performance of the service
retention.law: Limitation Act 1980 s. 5; Consumer Rights Act 2015 s. 19, 54
retention.note: No law makes a household keep receipts. A claim for faulty goods or a poor service is a contract claim, which must reach court within 6 years of the breach, usually delivery or performance. Keep a guarantee for its full term if longer, and everything until any complaint is settled. A card statement shows a purchase paid by credit card for a section 75 claim.

retention.title: Contracts and terms, notices given or received with proof of sending, and complaint letters (final responses, deadlock letters)
retention.title_pl: Umowy i regulaminy, wypowiedzenia wysłane i otrzymane wraz z dowodem nadania oraz korespondencja reklamacyjna (ostateczne odpowiedzi, pisma o impasie)
retention.from: the end of the contract or the settlement of the dispute, whichever is later
retention.law: Limitation Act 1980 s. 5 and 8; FCA Handbook DISP 2.8.2R
retention.note: Contract claims: 6 years from the breach (s. 5); a contract made by deed, such as a mortgage deed: 12 years (s. 8). The Financial Ombudsman Service needs the referral within 6 months of the final response and looks at complaints made to the firm within 6 years of the event or 3 years of becoming aware, so keep the dated final response letter.

retention.title: Insurance policies, schedules, renewal notices and claim correspondence
retention.title_pl: Polisy ubezpieczeniowe, wykazy warunków (schedule), zawiadomienia o odnowieniu i korespondencja w sprawie szkód
retention.from: the end of the cover or the closing of a claim, whichever is later
retention.note: A claim against the insurer under the policy is a contract claim (6 years). The renewal notice shows last year's premium (FCA Handbook ICOBS 6.5.1R), which helps check the next renewal price.

retention.title: Policies with liability cover: motor insurance, and home insurance with personal liability cover
retention.title_pl: Polisy z ubezpieczeniem odpowiedzialności cywilnej: ubezpieczenie komunikacyjne oraz ubezpieczenie domu z OC w życiu prywatnym
retention.from: receipt
retention.note: Suggestion. A personal injury claim can be brought within 3 years of the injury or of the injured person's date of knowledge, whichever is later (s. 11(4)); for an injured child, time runs only from age 18 (s. 28 with s. 38(2)). Such a claim can arrive long after the policy ended, and the old policy shows who covered it.

retention.title: Tenancy agreement or written statement of terms, deposit protection certificate and prescribed information, inventory, rent receipts, notices, and gas and electrical safety records received
retention.title_pl: Umowa najmu lub pisemne zestawienie warunków, certyfikat ochrony kaucji z informacjami wymaganymi, protokół zdawczo-odbiorczy, potwierdzenia zapłaty czynszu, wypowiedzenia oraz otrzymane protokoły bezpieczeństwa gazowego i elektrycznego
retention.from: the end of the tenancy or the return of the deposit, whichever is later
retention.law: Limitation Act 1980 s. 5 and 9; Housing Act 2004 s. 213, 214
retention.note: A tenant's court claim for a deposit not protected in time, or given without the prescribed information, can be made after the tenancy ends (s. 214) and is a claim for a sum recoverable by statute (6 years, s. 9). Contract claims about the tenancy also run 6 years (s. 5).

retention.title: Gas safety records, for a household that lets a home
retention.title_pl: Protokoły kontroli bezpieczeństwa gazowego (gas safety record), dla gospodarstwa wynajmującego mieszkanie
retention.from: the date of the check
retention.law: Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 reg. 36(3)(c)
retention.note: Keep each record until two further checks of the appliance or flue have been made; for an appliance or flue removed from the home, 2 years from its last check. Checks are at most 12 months apart, so this is about 2 years.

retention.title: Electrical installation condition reports, for a household that lets a home
retention.title_pl: Protokoły z kontroli instalacji elektrycznej (EICR), dla gospodarstwa wynajmującego mieszkanie
retention.from: the date of the inspection and test
retention.law: Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector and Social Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 reg. 3(3)(ca)
retention.note: Keep the report until the later of the date the next inspection is due (at most 5 years, sooner if the report says so) and the date it is done; a copy goes to the person doing the next inspection (reg. 3(3)(d)).

retention.title: Birth, adoption, marriage, civil partnership and death certificates
retention.title_pl: Odpisy aktów urodzenia, przysposobienia, małżeństwa, związku partnerskiego i zgonu
retention.from: receipt
retention.note: No law sets a period for a household. They serve as evidence in later applications, for example for a passport or Child Benefit. Copies can be ordered again from the General Register Office or the local register office, for a fee (gov.uk 'Order a copy of a birth, death or marriage certificate').

retention.title: Vehicle log book (V5C)
retention.title_pl: Dowód rejestracyjny pojazdu (V5C)
retention.from: while the household is the registered keeper
retention.law: Road Vehicles (Registration and Licensing) Regulations 2002 reg. 18 and 22
retention.note: No period is set, but the V5C is used to report a new address and a sale. On a sale the green new keeper slip goes to the buyer, and after telling DVLA online the rest is destroyed (gov.uk). A replacement costs £25 (reg. 18(1A) and 22(3)).

retention.title: MOT test certificates
retention.title_pl: Zaświadczenia o badaniu technicznym pojazdu (MOT)
retention.from: the test date
retention.note: Suggestion: keep the current certificate until the next test. Results are entered in the MOT database, and copies of current and previous certificates for tests in Great Britain can be downloaded (gov.uk 'Check MOT history').

retention.title: Old (cancelled) passports after renewal
retention.title_pl: Stare (unieważnione) paszporty po wymianie
retention.from: cancellation
retention.note: HM Passport Office cancels the old passport when it issues the new one; a cancelled British passport has the top right-hand corner of the cover cut off. A holder who does not want it back may ask for it to be destroyed (HMPO guidance 'Cancelling British passports', v23.0, 24 Aug 2026). No period is set; keep it only while it may still serve as evidence, for example of past travel.

retention.title: Health papers kept at home: vaccination records, hospital letters, NHS exemption and prepayment certificates
retention.title_pl: Dokumenty zdrowotne przechowywane w domu: szczepienia, listy ze szpitala, zaświadczenia o zwolnieniu z opłat i karnety na leki (PPC)
retention.from: receipt
retention.note: No law sets a period for a household. The GP and hospitals hold the full record, and a copy can be requested free of charge through a subject access request (UK GDPR Art. 12(5) and Art. 15). Keep exemption and prepayment certificates at least until they expire, because a wrongful claim for free prescriptions can lead to a penalty charge (NHSBSA HC11).

retention.title: School reports, and school offer, refusal and appeal letters
retention.title_pl: Okresowe raporty szkolne oraz pisma o przyznaniu lub odmowie miejsca w szkole i o odwołaniu
retention.from: receipt
retention.note: No law sets a period for parents. Suggestion: keep until the child leaves school. A refusal letter states the appeal deadline (School Admission Appeals Code 2022 para. 2.5).

retention.title: Inheritance Tax account, estate valuations and proof of tax paid (for personal representatives)
retention.title_pl: Rozliczenie podatku od spadku (Inheritance Tax), wyceny majątku spadkowego i dowody zapłaty podatku (dla zarządców spadku)
retention.from: the later of the date the tax (or the last instalment) was paid and accepted and the date it was due
retention.note: After 4 years HMRC cannot recover more tax paid on a delivered account; 6 years if the loss was careless, 20 years if deliberate. Where tax was not paid on a delivered account, for example an estate treated as excepted that was not, the limit is 20 years from the death, unless the loss was deliberate (s. 240(6) and (7)).

tasks.title: Tax the vehicle before driving it, or declare it off the road (SORN); tax does not pass from the seller
tasks.title_pl: Opłać podatek drogowy (vehicle tax) przed jazdą albo zgłoś pojazd jako wycofany z ruchu (SORN); podatek nie przechodzi od sprzedającego
tasks.law: Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994 s. 29(1), (2B) and (4), s. 31A
tasks.note: Use the reference number on the green new keeper slip.

tasks.title: Insure the vehicle before driving it
tasks.title_pl: Ubezpiecz pojazd (OC) przed pierwszą jazdą
tasks.law: Road Traffic Act 1988 s. 143(1) and (2), s. 144A, s. 144B
tasks.note: A registered vehicle must stay insured unless an exception applies, such as a vehicle kept off the road after notification.

tasks.title: Get the green new keeper slip; the seller tells DVLA of the sale
tasks.title_pl: Odbierz zielony odcinek dowodu V5C dla nowego właściciela; sprzedający zgłasza sprzedaż w DVLA
tasks.law: Road Vehicles (Registration and Licensing) Regulations 2002 reg. 22(2) and (5)
tasks.note: DVLA then sends the new V5C to the buyer; see window v5c-not-received.

tasks.title: Check that a car first registered 3 or more years ago has a current MOT
tasks.title_pl: Sprawdź, czy samochód zarejestrowany co najmniej 3 lata temu ma ważne badanie techniczne (MOT)
tasks.law: Road Traffic Act 1988 s. 47(1) and (2)
tasks.note: Test results are online (gov.uk 'Check MOT history').

tasks.title: Tell DVLA of the sale at once, online or by post, with the buyer's name and address and the sale date
tasks.title_pl: Niezwłocznie zgłoś sprzedaż w DVLA, online lub pocztą, podając imię, nazwisko i adres kupującego oraz datę sprzedaży
tasks.law: Road Vehicles (Registration and Licensing) Regulations 2002 reg. 22(2)(b); Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994 s. 59
tasks.note: After telling DVLA online, destroy the rest of the V5C (gov.uk).

tasks.title: Give the buyer the green new keeper slip
tasks.title_pl: Przekaż kupującemu zielony odcinek dowodu V5C dla nowego właściciela
tasks.law: Road Vehicles (Registration and Licensing) Regulations 2002 reg. 22(2)(a)
tasks.note: The buyer needs it to tax the vehicle.

tasks.title: Vehicle tax refund and cancellation of the Direct Debit happen automatically
tasks.title_pl: Zwrot podatku drogowego i anulowanie polecenia zapłaty następują automatycznie
tasks.law: Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994 s. 19(3)(f), (3A) and (7)
tasks.note: For each full month left, counted from the date DVLA gets the information.

tasks.title: Change or cancel the motor insurance
tasks.title_pl: Zmień lub wypowiedz ubezpieczenie samochodu
tasks.law: Policy terms (no statutory rule)
tasks.note: No statute sets a notice to the insurer on a sale.

tasks.title: Council tax: tell the councils for the old and the new address
tasks.title_pl: Podatek lokalny (council tax): powiadom urząd (council) właściwy dla starego i nowego adresu
tasks.law: Local Government Finance Act 1992 s. 2(1), s. 6(1) and (2)
tasks.note: Liability is worked out day by day and falls on the resident.

tasks.title: Register to vote at the new address
tasks.title_pl: Zarejestruj się w spisie wyborców pod nowym adresem
tasks.law: Representation of the People Act 1983 s. 9E(4) and (7); Representation of the People (England and Wales) Regulations 2001 reg. 23
tasks.note: Registration does not move with the household (gov.uk 'Register to vote').

tasks.title: Change the address on the driving licence
tasks.title_pl: Zmień adres w prawie jazdy (DVLA)
tasks.law: Road Traffic Act 1988 s. 99(4), (5) and (7)
tasks.note: Free; gov.uk gives a fine of up to £1,000 for not doing it. Driving is allowed while waiting.

tasks.title: Change the address on the vehicle log book (V5C)
tasks.title_pl: Zmień adres w dowodzie rejestracyjnym pojazdu (V5C)
tasks.law: Road Vehicles (Registration and Licensing) Regulations 2002 reg. 18(1); Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994 s. 59
tasks.note: Usually free; gov.uk gives a fine of up to £1,000. If the tax is due within 4 weeks, tax first with the current V5C.

tasks.title: Move the TV Licence to the new address
tasks.title_pl: Przenieś abonament telewizyjny (TV Licence) na nowy adres
tasks.law: Communications (Television Licensing) Regulations 2004 Sch. 1
tasks.note: A licence covers the place named in it; the address is updated with TV Licensing (gov.uk 'TV Licence').

tasks.title: Update the address with HMRC through the online account
tasks.title_pl: Zaktualizuj adres w HMRC przez konto online
tasks.law: Guidance: gov.uk 'Tell HMRC you've changed your address'
tasks.note: Only after the move. Covers Income Tax, National Insurance, Child Benefit and State Pension; business tax is updated separately.

tasks.title: Register with a GP near the new home
tasks.title_pl: Zapisz się do przychodni lekarza rodzinnego (GP) w pobliżu nowego domu
tasks.law: Guidance: nhs.uk 'How to register with a GP surgery'
tasks.note: No ID or proof of address is needed; the old surgery is told automatically.

tasks.title: Apply for an in-year school place
tasks.title_pl: Złóż wniosek o miejsce w szkole w trakcie roku szkolnego
tasks.law: School Admissions Code 2021 paras. 2.23 and 2.25 (England)
tasks.note: Through the council or the school, as the council's website explains. Wales has its own code.

tasks.title: Optional: Royal Mail redirection of post
tasks.title_pl: Opcjonalnie: przekierowanie poczty przez Royal Mail
tasks.law: No statutory duty
tasks.note: A paid Royal Mail service.

tasks.title: Check the baby's NHS number and register the baby with a GP
tasks.title_pl: Sprawdź numer NHS dziecka i zapisz je do lekarza rodzinnego (GP)
tasks.law: Guidance: nhs.uk 'What is an NHS number?'
tasks.note: The number is assigned soon after birth; no application is needed.

tasks.title: Give the employer paternity leave notices: entitlement by the 15th week before the expected week, each period at least 28 days ahead
tasks.title_pl: Złóż pracodawcy zawiadomienia o urlopie ojcowskim: o uprawnieniu do 15. tygodnia przed przewidywanym tygodniem porodu, o każdym okresie co najmniej 28 dni wcześniej
tasks.law: Paternity and Adoption Leave Regulations 2002 reg. 6(1) to (4)
tasks.note: Statutory Paternity Pay from 6 Apr 2026: £194.32 a week or 90% of average weekly earnings, whichever is lower; it needs 26 weeks' service by the qualifying week (Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992 s. 171ZA; Statutory Paternity Pay (General) Regulations 2002 reg. 2).

tasks.title: Shared Parental Leave: written notices at least 8 weeks before the first period
tasks.title_pl: Wspólny urlop rodzicielski (Shared Parental Leave): pisemne zawiadomienia co najmniej 8 tygodni przed pierwszym okresem
tasks.law: Shared Parental Leave Regulations 2014 reg. 8(1), reg. 12(3)
tasks.note: The mother's notice of entitlement and intention, and each parent's period of leave notice.

tasks.title: Free NHS prescriptions in England: apply for a maternity exemption certificate
